evals.prompt: I'm instrumenting a Java service with Byte Buddy. My AgentBuilder listener says it transformed com.example.AuthService, but my @Advice.OnMethodEnter logs never print. The advice calls AgentLog.debug from a nested helper class in the agent jar. How should I debug this without guessing?
evals.expected_output: Should separate transform success from advice execution, recommend a JDK-only first-pass advice body, identify helper class-loader visibility as a likely cause, and propose explicit next checks before richer logging.

evals.prompt: On Java 25 my Java agent is throwing Byte Buddy class-file version warnings, and constructor advice with onThrowable fails during transform. I still need a safe observer to understand object construction flow in an authorized lab app. What should I do first?
evals.expected_output: Should mention Byte Buddy/Java version compatibility, the possible need for documented experimental flags or upgrading Byte Buddy, constructor advice constraints, avoiding constructor onThrowable initially, and proving a normal method or entry-only observer first.

evals.prompt: We have authorization to reverse engineer a plugin-heavy JVM application. There are custom child-first class loaders, and I want to add method-entry tracing without destabilizing the app or leaking private data. Give me a disciplined plan.
evals.expected_output: Should state the authorization/safety boundary, keep observation minimal, map class loaders, use helper-free JDK-only logging first, define helper injection strategy only after execution is proven, and produce a report structure with transform and advice evidence separated.
